content:
If sentiment is positive and forecast is trending up, reduce forecast by 1–2% in early horizon to avoid overconfidence.  
If sentiment is negative and forecast is trending down, increase forecast by 1–2% in mid horizon to counteract pessimism.  
If sentiment is neutral and forecast deviates >3% from recent history, apply a 1–3% correction toward historical mean in late horizon.  
When sentiment swings from positive to negative within 5 days, reduce forecast slope by 15–25% in mid horizon.  
If sentiment is consistently positive over 3+ days and forecast is flat, add 0.5–1.5% upward bias in late horizon.  
If sentiment is negative and forecast is above recent high, cap forecast at 1.5–2.0% below recent peak in early horizon.
